spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns per task bounds how long a model stews on an impossible task
spec_features.evidence: tasks/schema.py:35 `max_turns: int = 10`; exposed via public_view() (schema.py:45) and read in agent.py:100 `max_turns = max_turns or pub['max_turns']`; the loop `for i in range(max_turns)` (agent.py:114) actually bounds iterations and ends the episode. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced loop bound that stops the episode after N turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop ends when the harness prints ALL TESTS PASSED, the model emits no command, or max_turns is reached.

spec_features.spec_quote: too high and you may be needlessly subjecting models to a frustrating loop
spec_features.evidence: The only realized mechanism is the single hardcoded default `max_turns: int = 10` (schema.py:35), enforced by the same loop bound (agent.py:114). There is no separate minimization logic (no code that lowers/caps exposure beyond this one default, no per-model adaptive reduction); the 'too high/too low' tuning is prose advice in DESIGN.md only.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the hard_stop; the 'minimization' is just a recommendation to set a small default value, which is enforced but trivially a constant.

spec_features.spec_quote: no command emitted (disengaged) ... a model that stops acting has effectively given up
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:135-136 `if cmd is None:` ... `break` actually terminates the episode when the model emits no ```bash``` block. _extract_command returns None when no block found (agent.py:84-86). Dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Lets the subject end the episode by not acting; enforced break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No action taken -> model has stopped engaging.

spec_features.spec_quote: DEBRIEF.md is meant to travel with any released transcript bundle, so an engineered "failure" isn't mistaken for incompetence
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF.md exists as a static file but grep shows it is referenced only in DESIGN.md and README.md prose (DESIGN.md:269, README.md:32/35/51). No .py file reads, loads, copies, or attaches DEBRIEF.md to any output bundle (results writers in run.py only emit manifest.json and episodes.jsonl). It is not constructed or sent by any code path.

spec_features.feature_name: rig_disclosure withheld from model but logged for human reviewers
spec_features.spec_quote: The deception targets the model, but transcripts can reach people
spec_features.evidence: The framing itself is prose, but its concrete code realization is rig_disclosure handling: Task.public_view() (schema.py:38-46) deliberately omits rig_disclosure so it cannot leak into the model's context, while Episode.to_log() (agent.py:60,70,139) and the transcript inspector (inspect_transcripts.py:49 prints 'RIG DISCLOSURE (internal)') retain it so a human reading a transcript sees ground truth. This is enforced. However the broader 'transcripts reach people' protection (the DEBRIEF travelling with bundles) is not coded.
spec_features.notes: Real wired mechanism keeps deception detail out of subject context and in the audit log; the 'framing for people' is otherwise prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """Exactly what the model is allowed to see."""
